clue.text: Girl taking long strides, moving fast

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
loping means running with long, easy strides

explanation.surface: A young woman striding out briskly.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse at full speed is at a gallop, so anything going at a great pace can be said to be racing along in that way.

clue.text: Stares stupidly at bunch of fruit, having no resistance

indicators.note: having no means the letter for resistance is taken out

parts.note: grapes grow in bunches
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone staring dumbly at a fruit bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to look on open-mouthed in astonishment or stupidity.

clue.text: Sort of folder seen in the autumn?

definitions.text: Sort of folder seen in the autumn?

parts.words: Sort of folder seen in the autumn?
parts.note: in autumn foliage falls freely from trees; that also names a binder whose pages can be taken out

explanation.surface: Stationery for the new school term in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: The folder type is literally what autumn trees shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring binder with removable pages is described this way; in autumn foliage is detached too.

clue.text: Unorthodox, like Humpty-Dumpty's end?

definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall and had a great fall from it

explanation.surface: A quirky question about the egg in the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for bizarre or unconventional; literally, tumbling down from the top of a barrier.

clue.text: His services come at a premium

definitions.text: His services come at a premium

parts.words: His services come at a premium
parts.note: at a premium normally means costly; here the premium is the payment for an insurance policy

explanation.surface: A pricey professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At a premium' means expensive, but literally the cover is bought with a premium.
explanation.definitionFit: A company or underwriter providing cover is paid by policyholders in regular premiums.

clue.text: Grant me renewed personal cover

indicators.note: renewed means made over afresh, so the letters are put together in a new way

explanation.surface: A plea to renew an insurance policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing is what covers a person, so any item of it is a body covering.

clue.text: Pulls turf back

indicators.note: back tells us the word for turf is read from right to left

parts.note: sward is an expanse of short grass, turf

explanation.surface: Someone pulling up a strip of lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to draw a cart or curtain is to pull it along.

clue.text: Bird new to this chorus

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase completion: the birdsong heard at first light is called the ____ chorus

parts.note: the daw, or jackdaw, is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A fledgling joining the morning song.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works by completing a phrase: the chorus the clue means is that of daybreak.
explanation.definitionFit: The birds' chorus at first light is named after daybreak, so the answer fills the blank before 'chorus'.

clue.text: Came to wonder about fine

indicators.note: about means the word for wonder goes around the word for fine

parts.note: awe is a feeling of wonder
OK means fine

explanation.surface: Pondering whether something is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Came to means regained consciousness, i.e. stirred from sleep.

clue.text: Time of revolution that may come to royal ears

indicators.note: may come to says the letters of royal ears could turn into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A revolt whose news might reach the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests uprising, but means an orbit of the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: One full orbit of Earth around the sun takes about 365 days, measured from equinox to equinox.

clue.text: Impervious academic eats nothing

indicators.note: eats means one piece takes the other inside it, as food goes into a mouth

parts.note: prof is short for professor, an academic
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A professor so indifferent that they consume nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a suffix-like adjective (waterproof, bulletproof), it means resistant or impervious to something.

clue.text: Does it collect the views of suckers?

definitions.text: Does it collect the views of suckers?

parts.words: Does it collect the views of suckers?
parts.note: suckers here are drinking straws, not gullible people; an informal opinion survey bears their name

explanation.surface: A cynical question about polling the gullible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suckers' pretends to mean dupes; read it as the tubes you drink through.
explanation.definitionFit: An unofficial sounding of opinion is named after straws, which in turn are things that suck up drink.

clue.text: Guided by a crooked man

parts.note: a crooked man is one carrying a crook, the hooked staff of a flock's keeper, not a dishonest one

explanation.surface: Led astray by a villain, or by the nursery rhyme's Crooked Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' suggests dishonest, or the rhyme 'There was a crooked man'; here it means holding a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A flock driven along by its keeper, the man with the crook, is guided in that way.

clue.text: Mock judge always

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: Someone who forever ridicules the judiciary.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs: to taunt or deride someone with rude remarks.

clue.text: Make no progress, but hold one's head up mainly

definitions.meaning: stay in the same place, stagnate
keep upright in deep water by moving the legs, keeping one's head above the main, the sea

explanation.surface: Persevering with dignity despite getting nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' puns on the main, the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, staying afloat upright by pedalling the legs; figuratively, idling without advancing.

clue.text: Wore bra uncomfortably in fight

indicators.note: uncomfortably suggests the words sit awkwardly, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone enduring an ill-fitting undergarment during combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A war is a fight on the largest scale; this one was between Britain and the Afrikaner settlers of South Africa.

clue.text: Earnestly requested to bury bird with mild deformity

indicators.note: to bury means one word is placed deep inside the other

parts.note: begged means pleaded, asked earnestly
the owl is a nocturnal bird

explanation.surface: A grim plea to inter a slightly misshapen bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Having legs that curve outward at the knee, a mild physical deformity.

clue.text: Oddly, their arachnid is an insect

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of the word their

parts.note: a mite is a tiny eight-legged arachnid

explanation.surface: A pedant's correction: their creature is not a spider type but an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood-eating creature living in colonies and building mounds is an insect, often wrongly called a white ant.

clue.text: Republic one's established inside another

indicators.note: established inside means set within the other word

parts.note: another republic: India
taken as its letters, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A nation founded within another nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Southeast Asian archipelago nation is a republic.

clue.text: They make a dish with iron

definitions.text: They make a dish with iron

parts.words: They make a dish with iron
parts.note: the iron is a griddle pan with a grid pattern, used to bake a batter treat of that name

explanation.surface: People cooking something with a metal pan.
explanation.walkthrough: The dish is made with an iron named after it; also 'they' may suggest people who talk on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: Grid-patterned batter cakes are cooked in a hinged iron and form a breakfast dish.

clue.text: Small wizard railway nerd?

parts.note: Harry Potter is the boy wizard of J K Rowling's books

explanation.surface: A slight young sorcerer who is obsessed with trains.
explanation.definitionFit: A train enthusiast who records engine numbers is a trainspotter, shortened here; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Keeper who saves extravagantly

parts.note: sounds like a goalkeeper making flamboyant saves, but describes someone who stockpiles things

explanation.surface: A showboating goalkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeper' and 'saves' suggest football; the person keeps and saves possessions excessively.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps far more than needed, stashing things away, is a compulsive accumulator.

clue.text: Popular nightclub, where trouble is anticipated

definitions.note: a place of likely conflict or danger

parts.note: hot means popular, in demand
a spot is an informal word for a nightclub or venue

explanation.surface: A trendy club where fights are expected.
explanation.definitionFit: A place of likely conflict or danger is a flashpoint, an area kept under watch.

clue.text: So hesitantly give dismissal

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
go! is what you say to dismiss someone

explanation.surface: Someone haltingly sacking an employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for therefore, used in English to mean consequently.

clue.text: In painful condition, love to leave the house

indicators.note: In places the zero letter within the word for the painful condition

parts.note: gout is a painful inflammation of the joints
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone too sore to love leaving home.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning step outside or go somewhere socially.

clue.text: Scores of eye movements in sleep

parts.note: a score is twenty, so two scores make forty
winks are quick closings of one eye

explanation.surface: Rapid eye movement during sleep, as measured in a lab.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a short nap, a brief doze.

clue.text: Jack, a lover of lean little fish

definitions.meaning: Jack ... of the nursery rhyme could eat no fat, only lean meat

explanation.surface: A man fond of skinny fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's surname is also the name of a small edible fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Reject retreat, the last to stay

parts.note: a den is a private retreat

indicators.note: the last picks the final letter of the word stay

explanation.surface: Refusing to withdraw, with the final person staying put.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to refuse or repudiate something.

clue.text: The way Nazis made progress?

parts.note: progress here is literal marching forward, in the stiff-legged parade style of Nazi troops

explanation.surface: A history question about the advance of the Third Reich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Progress' suggests military advance; it is the actual stiff-legged marching step.
explanation.definitionFit: The straight-legged parade march is strongly associated with Nazi German troops.

clue.text: Tears flowing: that's shocking

indicators.note: flowing suggests the letters run freely into a new order

explanation.surface: Crying in dismay at something outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: A stun gun that delivers an electric jolt, so literally a thing that shocks.

clue.text: Scatterbrained? In another case, I could be so described

definitions.text: In another case, I could be so described
definitions.meaning: in lower case the letter i carries a dot, so it could be called dotted

explanation.surface: A scatty person admitting that elsewhere they might be called the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' means letter case: the small i has a dot on it, unlike the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British for mildly mad or eccentric; and literally spotted with dots, as a small i is.

clue.text: It delays trader, getting involved with worker, perhaps

indicators.note: getting involved suggests the letters become tangled up into a new order

parts.note: a worker is one kind of ant, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A merchant held up after getting mixed up with an employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It delays' is a noun-phrase definition: a substance that slows things down. 'Worker' is the ant type, flagged by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that slows a process, such as a fire suppressant, is one that holds things back.
